text:
incidents-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx: edge gateway 502/504 spike detected (us-east-1, ap-south-1). 5xx rate 15% over last 4m. Paging primary oncall.

maya_sre: I'm awake, oncall accepted. hitting dashboards now. @tom_sre can you shadow? jess_ops please check if we have any recent edge config pushes.

tom_sre: here. no proxy binary deploys in last 2h. I see a surge in backend latencies and a ton of `upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out)` in edge logs.

jess_ops: only change was an autoscaling policy tweak for model-pool-21 about 90 minutes ago (lowered scale threshold), not a config push to edge proxies.

yun_infra: checking cloud LB metrics — SYN/EST handshake drops starting at 14:05 UTC. looks like backend TCP sockets are exhausted on some nodes, causing many 502s.

maya_sre: interesting. can you list which backend nodes are impacted and if they coincide with a single pool?

yun_infra: model-pool-21 has 6 nodes; two nodes show high TIME_WAIT/socket usage and a very high file descriptor count. grabbing `ss -s` and process fd counts.

tom_sre: on the edge side, nginx logs show repeated `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)`. suggests backend process crash or FD exhaustion.

jess_ops: I'm hitting the pods' logs: one of the model workers shows repeated `EMFILE: too many open files` errors and then a slow response pattern.

maya_sre: hypothesis: a regression in model runtime that leaked file descriptors and caused nodes to stop accepting new connections, which cascades to 502/504 at edge. Mitigation plan: 1) take affected backends out of rotation, 2) scale pool up and restart affected pods, 3) adjust LB drain settings to faster remove unhealthy nodes.

jess_ops: can do: `kubectl label pod -n inference <pod-xyz> evict=now` then `edge-admin pool drain model-pool-21 --region=us-east --grace=5s`.

yun_infra: starting drain + eviction now. creating autoscaler override to add 4 nodes temporarily (command: `autoscaler set-min model-pool-21 10`).

incidentbot: pool-drain job queued: job-3214, started by jess_ops at 2034567945.

maya_sre: while that's happening, increase proxy keepalive timeout to avoid premature resets: `nginx: keepalive_timeout 65s` and reduce upstream fail_timeout to 3s for faster failover. will push via edge-config-canary.

tom_sre: watch out for retries amplifying errors. we should also temporarily disable aggressive client retries at the gateway to avoid thundering retries into bad backends.

jess_ops: applied autoscaler override and drained two affected nodes. new nodes are spinning up. pool shows 8/10 ready now.

yun_infra: nodes up but pods on new nodes are Slow starting due to large model cold-start. starting a hot-warm restart: replace failing runtime with pre-warmed container image.

jess_ops: switched to prewarmed image for pool via `kubectl set image deployment/model-pool-21 model=runtime:prewarm-20260314`.

maya_sre: good. posting a short status update: "Investigating increased 5xx errors; we are removing unhealthy backend nodes and scaling the pool. Some requests may see higher latency or errors. More updates in 10 minutes." status-bot link draft prepared.

status-bot: Status draft saved: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2034567890/draft

tom_sre: monitoring suggests error rate dropping from 15% -> 6% after first drain. still seeing intermittent 504s from long backend tail.

maya_sre: does the runtime expose per-request memory/KV cache size? maybe certain requests cause workers to block. capture slow requests from access logs and tail worker logs.

jess_ops: collected slow request samples and `strace` dump of failing process; we see many `epoll_wait` stalls followed by `EMFILE` errors. pushing a kernel-level fix: increase `fs.file-max` and per-process `ulimit -n` as a temporary stopgap.

yun_infra: increased ulimit for runtime service via DaemonSet patch and bumped node-level `fs.file-max`. also adding a firewall rule tweak to drop half-open timeouts quicker.

maya_sre: after these changes, graphs show 5xx at 2.2% at 2034568120. continue to monitor for 30m. if stable, we'll remove autoscaler override and revert nginx keepalive sooner.

tom_sre: agree. prepare artifacts for postmortem: kernel metrics, pod logs, access logs, autoscaler event history, config commits. assigning postmortem to yun_infra.

yun_infra: taking postmortem. starting to gather artifacts to `gs://redwood-incidents/2034567890/`.

jess_ops: publishing status update: "Mitigation in progress: unhealthy backend nodes removed and pool scaled; errors decreasing. We will follow up with a postmortem." published link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2034567890

incident-bot: mitigation action completed: pool scaled to 10, 2 bad nodes drained at 2034568050.

maya_sre: error rate now 0.8% at 2034568180. marking as recovered but keep monitoring. let's schedule a short SOC sync in 24h for follow-ups.

tom_sre: one follow-up: add circuit-breaker on proxy so unhealthy backends are tripped earlier; file a ticket with runtime team to fix FD leak. i'll create the ticket.

yun_infra: creating postmortem stub and linking artifacts. assigning remediation tasks: increase default ulimit for runtime, add canary for runtime memory/fd regression, add latency-based autoscaling rule.

status-bot: Incident update: Resolved - error rates returned to acceptable levels. Postmortem in progress: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2034567890/postmortem

maya_sre: summary: root cause likely FD leak in runtime causing node exhaustion -> backend pod failures -> edge 502/504 amplification via retries. Remediations planned and assigned. Thanks everyone.

jess_ops: I'll stay on shadow for 30m. closing channel after monitoring period. :thumbsup:
